title: One lead leg contributes
effort: Apply force through either lead leg while preserving a forward line and controlled support.
quality_marker: Within E1 record controlled split-start projections separately for each lead leg: front foot loaded, no twist, feet parallel at reception and a quiet 2 s hold. Record all four attempts per lead; no weak side is inferred before actual data exists. Use the listed attempts only; a miss or invalid attempt consumes the dose. Record actual attempts, setup and any substitutions; no bonus tests or comparison across unlike tasks.
brief: The split-start broad jump keeps two-foot takeoff/reception but biases initiation toward one lead leg. Single-leg hip and ankle tasks isolate contributors; grounded step-up coordination and a small scoop connect them. Two short starts provide limited acceleration practice, not maximum-speed development.

explosive.name: Split-Stance Broad Jump — fixed lead, two-foot reception
explosive.key: Split-Stance Broad Jump — fixed lead, two-foot reception
explosive.job: Main asymmetric leg contribution to a forward push while retaining a bilateral landing.
explosive.cue: Start in a modest split stance, front whole foot loaded and rear foot assisting. Use one small dip and project a short distance; land with feet parallel and hold 2 s. Repeat with the other lead leg; this is not a single-leg takeoff.
explosive.replacement: a shorter split-stance jump, or the Week 1 parallel broad jump if asymmetry loses the forward line; record the changed start
explosive.identity: standing-broad-jump parent; split-start bilateral takeoff/floor reception proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Changes which leg contributes most at initiation without adding single-leg reception. A same-leg forward hop was rejected because stance-force isolation does not require its landing demand.
explosive.rest_text: 90 s between complete set rounds; complete one leg's bout, rest 60 s, then the other leg; 8 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Glute Bridge — single-leg rapid rise with level pelvis
explosive.key: Glute Bridge — single-leg rapid rise with level pelvis
explosive.job: Express hip extension on each side without the second leg hiding pelvic control.
explosive.cue: One foot grounded, other thigh comfortably lifted; drive hips up quickly, hold 1 s, lower 2 s without twist. Use bodyweight and a short controllable range.
explosive.replacement: a kickstand-assisted rapid bridge at the same per-leg dose if the pelvis rotates; record assistance
explosive.identity: bodyweight-glute-bridge parent; unilateral rapid execution proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Related to bilateral rapid bridge, with independent hip/torso control. More load on the bilateral task would not answer this side-specific job.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 4 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Step-Up to Knee Drive — fast ascent, no flight
explosive.key: Step-Up to Knee Drive — fast ascent, no flight
explosive.job: Coordinate lead-leg extension with free-leg recovery while keeping the support foot planted.
explosive.cue: Use a low immovable step, lead whole foot planted. Rise quickly and bring the trailing knee forward to hip level only if balanced; hold 1 s, lower 3 s. No launch or jump from the top.
explosive.replacement: the Week 1 rapid step-up with the rear foot joining the support at the same per-leg dose when free-leg balance is unconfirmed
explosive.identity: step-up-to-knee-drive parent in jumping-distance-all-cards.json; nonflight rapid delivery proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Adds coordinated free-leg recovery, not merely a higher step. A step-up jump would add flight while obscuring this controlled support task.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 4 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Medicine Ball Scoop Toss — fixed split stance, forward release
explosive.key: Medicine Ball Scoop Toss — fixed split stance, forward release
explosive.job: Carry an asymmetric leg push into a free implement without another landing.
explosive.cue: Use a light ball between thighs and a small fixed split stance. Hinge slightly, drive through the feet to release forward/upward with long arms. No twist, step or catching return; perform two with each lead leg.
explosive.replacement: a parallel-stance hip scoop at the same total four throws if the split base twists; if containment fails, four unloaded rapid hip hinges with zero throws
explosive.identity: medicine-ball-scoop-toss parent; split-base nonrotational delivery proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Related scoop family; the asymmetric force-to-release problem supports today’s lead-leg effort without adding unilateral reception. A rotational throw was rejected as outside this course’s sagittal focus.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 4 total reps; 20 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Calf Raise — single-leg fast supported finish, no flight
explosive.key: Calf Raise — single-leg fast supported finish, no flight
explosive.job: Reveal each stance ankle’s fast plantar-flexion contribution without balance limiting it.
explosive.cue: Hold stable support, other foot off the floor; rise quickly on one forefoot, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Knee stays softly straight and heel aligned; no hop.
explosive.replacement: a lightly assisted single-leg rise at the same per-leg dose if the heel path slows or rolls
explosive.identity: single-leg-calf-raise parent; rapid nonflight delivery proposed
explosive.novelty_reason: Related to grounded bilateral ankle finish, now independently supported. Unilateral pogos were rejected because load acceptance is not the primary question.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 45 s, then the other leg; 6 total reps; 10 s between individual reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

explosive.name: Standing Split-Start Acceleration — 2 m, full stop
explosive.key: Standing Split-Start Acceleration — 2 m, full stop
explosive.job: Apply a lead-leg push to the first running steps and then regain control.
explosive.cue: Begin stationary in a comfortable split stance; push forward and accelerate for only 2 m, then decelerate within the final inspected 7 m after reserving 1 m for the start stance. One attempt with each lead leg. No jump start, fall or backward rock; use submaximal effort if needed to stop comfortably.
explosive.replacement: two fast grounded supported split-squat rises total, one per lead leg, when the running/stopping envelope is unsuitable; record zero sprint metres
explosive.identity: Proposed exact short-start coaching prescription; no timing-gate or maximum-speed test ID
explosive.novelty_reason: First short locomotor application, with only two starts. Another jumping variation would add landing volume while missing first-step force transfer.
explosive.rest_text: complete one leg's bout, rest 90 s, then the other leg; 2 total reps; 90 s before the next exercise/section

resilience.job: Light inner-ankle strengthening to organize the foot arch without toe clawing.
resilience.cue: Heel supported; hand-held light band draws the forefoot outward. Move forefoot inward 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s with shin still.
resilience.replacement: gentle hand resistance through a smaller range at the same per-leg dose
resilience.identity: Proposed exact dynamic execution; no exact canonical ID

resilience.job: Light lateral-hip strengthening to keep the pelvis and knee organized over the force-producing leg.
resilience.cue: Lie on side, lower leg bent; lift upper leg slightly 2 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s with toes facing forward and pelvis still. Bodyweight is sufficient unless clearly easy.
resilience.replacement: a smaller unloaded leg lift with the same per-leg dose

E: Use light resistance or bodyweight that permits visibly rapid force with control. Begin with E1 while fresh. Each row has a distinct job; supporting work stays small. Rest may be extended to 2–3 minutes when speed, control or attention has not returned. Stop for pain, loss of alignment, stiff/asymmetric landing or clear slowing; rest and regress remaining work only if control returns, otherwise record stopped work. Never make up failed attempts. No drop landings or rotational throws are prescribed.
S: Light controlled strengthening, at least 5 technical reps in reserve. Do not chase burn, shaking or pre-fatigue. Reduce load/range when control fades; stop for symptoms.
P: Working sets are challenging at about 2–3 technical reps/cycles in reserve. Select load/lever from demonstrated ability, not age or calendar week. Keep the stated controlled lowering and complete range; no forced repetitions, maximum testing or conditioning circuit. Check late-set and late-session quality; record reductions instead of forcing nominal completion.

setup: Inspect the split takeoff and receiving corridor. The two 2 m starts reserve the first 1 m for the starting stance, accelerate from 1 m to 3 m and need the final 7 m clear for deceleration; if the actual athlete cannot stop within it, use the listed grounded replacement. Running foot strikes are not counted as jump landings; record actual running contacts only if measured. Inspect stable supports, minimum loads, surface grip and all active/waiting/return paths. Keep one athlete active per lane under suitable supervision; no group size or station count is assumed. Three separate 10 m lanes are not a 30 m runway. Ball releases need separately verified flight/bounce/roll containment. Replacements occupy the original slot; missing readiness or equipment can change the practice exposure and actual totals. Braking travel, ordinary running foot strikes and walking returns are not jump contacts or the recorded accelerating metres; actual distances/steps remain unknown and must be logged if measured. Mark the entire start/drive/stop envelope inside the lane: front starting foot at 1 m, trailing foot inside the first metre, drive to 3 m and stop by 10 m. Shorten effort or use the grounded replacement if the stance or stopping margin does not fit. Before applying multiple replacements, check the other rows: a replacement must not duplicate an exercise already delivered in another slot. Do not add duplicate work just to fill the count. If the supplied replacements cannot preserve distinct jobs, stop the affected slot and record a modified/incomplete session for revision; do not claim the planned six distinct explosive tasks were completed. Changed reset time, takeoff/landing type, sides and reps belong in the actual record.
delivery: Estimate 64–71 minutes after Access & Prepare 1 for an athlete with equipment access. Includes work, resets, listed recovery, preparation, transitions and 10–16 minutes of extra instruction/setup; additional queues, rest or load-finding add time. Existing preparation duration and total booking fit remain unresolved. Never compress needed recovery to fit a clock. One coached focus class per week for twelve weeks. Review actual sport, leg lifting, running, jumping and tumbling before delivery. Initially allow roughly 48–72 hours before another demanding leg exposure when the full schedule permits, adjusting to actual recovery; a week elapsed is not proof of readiness. Resume missed classes without doubling up. No additional full workouts or body-control blocks are prescribed.
progression: Week 2 used seven bilateral primary bouts. Here Split Squat becomes the priority at 2 × 5 per leg; RDL reduces to 1 × 6, Goblet Squat stays 1 × 6 and the bridge slot yields to the returning Split Squat while both calf-angle and hamstring jobs are retained. Seven rounds now require nine bouts, so this is not an equal-time dose merely because the round count matches. Choose loads for current split-stance control; no increase is earned. Advance only after both sides meet the stated technique/reserve and actual recovery is satisfactory.
audit_findings: Eight bilateral receptions arise from an asymmetric start, not eight unilateral landings. Four scoop throws and two 2 m starts are separate exposure types. All six drills relate to the lead-leg goal; related families are openly labeled. Extra unilateral bouts are offset by reduced RDL and squat work; no repeated-hop block is added. Braking travel, ordinary running foot strikes and walking returns are not jump contacts or the recorded accelerating metres; actual distances/steps remain unknown and must be logged if measured. Mark the entire start/drive/stop envelope inside the lane: front starting foot at 1 m, trailing foot inside the first metre, drive to 3 m and stop by 10 m. Shorten effort or use the grounded replacement if the stance or stopping margin does not fit.
